title: Multi-Year Comparative Techno-Economic Assessment of PV, Wind, and Hybrid Green Hydrogen Systems: Case Studies in Myanmar
content: Myanmar’s renewable resources could support green-hydrogen production, but evidence on how location, hourly variability, and system configuration influence performance remains limited. This study compares PV-only, wind-only, and hybrid PV–wind systems at five Myanmar locations. Hourly ERA5 data for 2015–2025 were converted into renewable-electricity profiles and supplied to a 10 MW proton-exchange-membrane electrolyser model. For each location, weather year, and cost scenario, 48 discrete renewable-capacity designs were evaluated through hourly dispatch, hydrogen production, electrolyser utilisation, curtailment, and plant-gate levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH). PV capacity factors varied little among locations, while wind capacity factors exhibited greater spatial and interannual variability. Under the central cost case, Minbu consistently selected 15 MW PV, whereas Ngapudaw, Seikphyu, and Wundwin consistently selected 15 MW PV plus 10 MW wind. Wundwin achieved the lowest mean LCOH (10.30 USD/kg) and highest mean annual hydrogen production (725.30 tonnes/year). Mean LCOH across all locations ranged from 6.53 to 13.94 USD/kg under the low and high cost cases. Fixed-design analysis showed robust performance at four locations; Sittwe incurred a mean penalty of 0.06 USD/kg. Hydrogen cost therefore depends jointly on resource complementarity, electrolyser utilisation, curtailment, and renewable-capacity cost.
